then.text: Pier Head, best backdrop in England. That's a fact. I checked. Twice.
If the Enclosure ever ask again, I'm going to say I'm busy. Doing a bit of... thinking.

else.text: Hey! Wow, you got here! I'm doing a live stream. Say hi to the viewers. All twelve of them.
It was fourteen, but two left when you waved.

then.text: {player}! Pier Head, golden hour, and the ferry horn is hitting perfectly. This is my best backdrop yet.
Chat's been saying I should 'let the Enclosure sponsor a battle'. I said I'd do it for free. For now.
Don't make a face. It's going in the highlights!

else.text: Right. The ferry horn was perfect, you were rubbish at lighting, and I still lost. Rude.
Go on, then. Keeper Ray is in the club up the road. Cavern-ish, loud, and he does a very good rimshot.

sailor.text: The ferry to Douglas leaves whenever the tide agrees. Fancy a trip across?

rail_guard.text: Lime Street. Mind the gap. And mind the seagulls.

then.text: In wind like this, I keep an eye on the Liver Birds. Still there. Phew.
Morning! Bella's watching the sea for the boats coming in. Bertie's having a lie-in.

liver_bird_fan.text: Up on the Liver Building sit two Liver Birds, Bella and Bertie. One looks over the city, one over the sea.
Legend says if they ever fly away, the city will cease to exist. Don't tell them there's a gull strike.

beatles_fan.text: The Beatles played the Cavern Club nearly 300 times between 1961 and 1963. Mostly lunchtimes.
That's one every three days, near enough. Meanwhile I can't even manage a Tuesday.

then.text: Rain on the Albert Dock bricks. They've seen worse since 1846. So have I, nearly.
Docks look lovely as the lights come on. The rum barrels would've loved it.

dock_historian.text: Albert Dock opened in 1846. It was the first dock complex in the world built without any wood, so no fires.
Now it's all museums and tea rooms. Same bricks, fewer rum barrels.

verger.text: Liverpool Cathedral is the largest cathedral in Britain. Took seventy-four years to build, from 1904.
The tower's one of the tallest cathedral towers anywhere. Do not try to dust it.

then.text: That wind's come straight off the Mersey, la. Hold onto your scran, it'll have it.
Bit of rain never hurt anyone. It's perfect weather for a big bowl of scouse.
Sun's out! Everyone's down the waterfront. Best city in the world when it's sunny, that.

scouser.text: {greeting} Scouse is a stew of beef, veg and spuds. The name comes from 'lobscouse', a sailor's meal.
We named ourselves after the stew. Not the other way round. Probably.

then.text: Choppy on the Mersey today. The ferry still goes. It's braver than me.
Can't see Birkenhead in this fog. It's still there, I checked the timetable.
Sunset over the Mersey from the ferry. Honestly, worth the fare twice.

ferry_fan.text: {greeting} Gerry and the Pacemakers sang 'Ferry Cross the Mersey' in 1964. Everyone on the boat has to hum it. It's the law.
The ferry's older than the song. And better at turning.

gate_wirral.text: This road to the Wirral is closed for Heritage Resurfacing.
It has been closed since this morning. It will reopen when someone more important than me says so.

else.text: I hear there's a Keeper in the club who knows someone more important. Just a rumour. I'm not here.

liverpool_deckhand.text: Last crossing to Birkenhead's gone, so it's ropes and a mop for me now.
The Mersey at night is all lights. The Liver Building glows like it's showing off.
Hear that? Foghorn out by the bar. Ships come in all night, the river never sleeps.

liverpool_astronomer.text: There's an old observatory on Bidston Hill, over the water. They used to set the ships' clocks from there.
Too many city lights for the faint stars here, but Jupiter shows up every time. Reliable lad, Jupiter.
Look, see that bright one over the river? That's not a star. That's a plane to Dublin.
